candidates.label: Benign ovarian mucinous cystadenoma
missing_or_uncertain: Elevated HE4 and LDH are non-specific but may be associated with large tumor burden

contradiction_refs: F10 (size >15 cm more typical of mucinous)
candidates.label: Benign ovarian serous cystadenoma
missing_or_uncertain: Serous cystadenomas are usually smaller; large size favors mucinous

contradiction_refs: F11 (no solid components or fat/calcifications typical of dermoid)
candidates.label: Mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst)
missing_or_uncertain: Presence of fat, hair, or calcifications not reported on imaging

candidates.label: Ovarian borderline tumor (mucinous borderline)
missing_or_uncertain: Histological assessment needed to exclude borderline features

candidates.label: Ovarian epithelial carcinoma (e.g., serous carcinoma)
missing_or_uncertain: Invasive cancer unlikely given imaging and tumor markers; HE4 elevation may be false positive or due to other causes

response.rationale: The two-year history of slow growth and imaging showing a large unilocular thin-walled cyst without solid components strongly favor a benign mucinous cystadenoma over serous cystadenoma or other entities. The elevated HE4 and LDH are non-specific and do not outweigh the reassuring imaging and normal CA-125. The absence of solid components and septations argues against teratoma, borderline tumor, and invasive carcinoma, which typically exhibit more complex features.
